extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications teams, and agency clients preparing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a checklist for writing, packaging, distributing, and measuring press releases that attract media pickup and SEO value. Includes pre-release checks, headline/lede/body/quote rules, distribution strategy, and measurement standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release is one tool, not the whole strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release is one tool, not the whole strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use releases as part of a broader campaign (multichannel, relationships, owned/social) rather than expecting them alone to achieve objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality over quantity in distribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize targeted, tier-appropriate placements and tailored outreach rather than mass-distributing many low-value releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia is now table stakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include photos, video, infographics, and other assets to increase pickup and engagement; multimedia should be prepared pre-release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder/executive voice differentiates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use senior/executive perspective (e.g., founder or CEO posts) to add distinct voice and credibility across channels like LinkedIn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term media relationships matter most
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate relationships with journalists and trade outlets; prioritize exclusives and coordinated outreach based on those relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness test: 'would I share at dinner?'
rubrics_metrics.description: News passes the "would I share at dinner?" test
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this informal litmus to assess whether the announcement is genuinely interesting or relevant to others before issuing a release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson briefed and available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a prepared, accessible spokesperson is ready for media follow-up and interviews at release time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia assets ready
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have high-quality, editable multimedia assets prepared and approved for press use to accompany the release and social kit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media kit prepared
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare shareable assets, suggested copy, and visuals for social channels to enable coordinated amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer/partner approvals secured
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain necessary approvals from mentioned customers or partners before publishing to avoid legal/relationship issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response plan if needed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a contingency plan and messaging ready in case the announcement triggers negative attention or unexpected issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal stakeholders briefed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform internal teams (sales, customer support, executives) about timing and messaging so they can respond consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: news-first, brand-second
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame headline around the news value rather than prioritizing the brand name; make the news hook front-and-center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline uses active voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headlines in active voice to be direct and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline includes concrete numbers when possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific figures, dates, or metrics in headlines to increase clarity and perceived newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline length limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headlines concise (≤80 characters) to improve readability and appearance in feeds and emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Tested with focus group of 3-5 people
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate headline effectiveness with a small internal/external sample to ensure clarity and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede condenses 5 W's into 50 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the lede, succinctly address who, what, when, where, why (and how if relevant) within ~50 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede leads with most newsworthy element
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the strongest, most relevant news hook at the start of the lede to capture attention immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede uses concrete details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific facts (numbers, dates, names) to substantiate claims and enable reporters to assess relevance quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede uses active voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid passive constructions in the lede to be direct and clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid throat-clearing language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate vague lead-ins or filler that delay the news (e.g., unnecessary background or qualifiers) in the lede.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body structure: inverted pyramid
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order information from most to least important so editors can trim from the bottom without losing the core story.

rubrics_metrics.name: One idea per paragraph
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep paragraphs focused and short to aid skimming and editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use subheaders for scannability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break text with descriptive subheads so readers and editors can quickly find relevant sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place a quote on the first page
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a compelling quote early in the release to provide human perspective and a pull-quote for journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include customer/partner proof point
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a customer or partner example or metric that validates the announcement and increases credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide methodology for data-based claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing survey or data findings, include brief methodology so reporters can judge rigor and reproduce context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote length guideline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep quoted remarks concise (about 25–35 words) so they are excerptable and usable in media copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote voice: spokesperson sounds human
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write quotes that feel authentic and conversational rather than corporate boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes should add new information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes contribute perspective or facts beyond what is in the lede/body rather than repeating it verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsubstantiated superlatives in quotes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use claims like "industry-leading" or "best" unless supported by evidence; risk sounding promotional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes must be excerptable independently
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft quotes that make sense out of context so journalists can lift them cleanly into coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoed exclusive to top trade publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed exclusive to top trade publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer an exclusive under embargo to a top trade outlet to secure prominent early coverage and deepen media relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated release to secondary outlets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan a staged outreach to a handful of secondary publications after an exclusive to broaden reach without flooding the market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use wire services for SEO after initial coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire for SEO (after initial coverage runs)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish to wire services to capture search/SEO value once primary coverage and exclusives have run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deploy social media kit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release social assets and suggested copy across channels in coordination with media outreach to amplify coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include newsletter placements where relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target industry or company newsletters that reach key audiences as part of the distribution plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder/CEO LinkedIn post
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have senior leaders share the announcement on LinkedIn to leverage personal networks and lend credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: coverage tiering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify pickups by tier (top national/trade outlets vs. secondary/local) to assess quality of coverage, not just volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: sentiment analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the tone of coverage to understand reputational impact, not only presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: brand mention tracking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and count brand mentions across outlets and channels to quantify visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: pickup velocity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how quickly outlets pick up the story (especially within the first 24 hours) as an indicator of resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: long-tail SEO impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organic search and referral traffic over a longer window (e.g., 90 days) to capture sustained SEO benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: news substantive enough for outside-org test
rubrics_metrics.description: News substantive enough for outside-org test
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release should have independent news value that an outside organization would consider worth sharing or covering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: multimedia ready
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia assets must be available and appropriate to support the story across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: spokesperson available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A ready spokesperson must be accessible for follow-up to convert interest into coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: tier-appropriate distribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution plan should match the news' significance, using exclusives and targeted outreach when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: coordinated cross-channel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release should be amplified across owned, earned, and paid channels in a coordinated way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: measurement beyond impressions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should include qualitative and business-relevant metrics (sentiment, tiers, pickup velocity, SEO), not just raw impression counts.
